Lone wanderer with bedroll and tin-cup, counting stars where cities once burned quietly.
Motorbike-courier with cargo-strap and goggles, delivering sealed letters nobody expected to arrive.
Former-soldier with patched-uniform jacket and rifle-slung, guarding a bridge she no longer remembers why.
Wandering-monk with rosary and worn-staff, blessing each empty town like it still held congregation.
Young orphan-scavenger with mechanical-dog companion, teaching it new tricks in crumbled shopping arcades.
Gunslinger drifter with revolver-holster and dust-coat, arriving just before trouble and leaving just after.
Postal-runner with satchel, carrying birthday cards addressed to towns erased from every surviving map.
Deserter-soldier with faded insignia, tending a rooftop garden nobody ordered her to plant.
Parts-scavenger with toolbelt and goggles, humming softly while rebuilding a radio nobody broadcasts on yet.
Shrine-keeper with broom and incense-tin, sweeping ash from steps the pilgrims stopped climbing years ago.
Map-cartographer sketching ruins on parchment, naming collapsed streets after flowers she imagines once grew there.
Field-medic with worn kit, walking clinic-to-clinic between settlements too small to appear on any chart.
Teen scavenger with drone-friend, arguing cheerfully with it over which collapsed tower holds better salvage.
Chart-maker with quadrant and steady hands, correcting pre-fall maps one honest measurement at a time.
Lone harmonica-player pausing at each junction, leaving a small melody in the dust before moving on.
Ex-pilot with cracked helmet clipped to pack, navigating on foot now with the same calm precision.
Herbalist with pouch of dried leaves, trading remedies for news and treating both with equal care.
Drifter with bedroll and compass, following river-roads between settlements nobody officially connected anymore.
Pre-fall historian with water-stained notebook, recording what people remember rather than what records insisted.
Young scavenger with compass and hand-drawn charts, adding pencil corrections older cartographers never got to make.
Retired marine with quiet hands, running a ferry across the flooded interchange, charging nothing, refusing thanks.
Two-person camp duo sharing one cook-pot, navigating by argument and arriving, somehow, exactly right.
Rifle-slung scout with dust-coat, marking safe water sources on a map she leaves at every waypost.
Nurse-wanderer with bandage-slung pack, moving between the small settlements where nobody else thought to stop.
Radio-relay carrier with patched antenna-rig, retransmitting voices across the silence so distance feels briefly smaller.
